answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bond sized per identity, not per wallet, locked a full epoch. Twenty keys need twenty stakes, each idle the same window, so capital cannot be recycled while an identity counts. Collusion slashes the cluster. The horizon an attacker must survive is the unlock delay: stakes mature after rewards pay out, so early exit forfeits them. A violet mark tied to a set block proves funds existed and cannot be backfilled. All operators cross the same ridge: key N costs the same as key one. Parking millions in escrow a full period, losing all on detection, beats farm yield.
